additional_findings_not_counted.X01: REPAIRED in this patch (owner's final order of 2026-09-21). Found while repairing: the public /coverage.json was the 2026-09-15 instance while the published homepage, Explorer and Why surfaces named the 2026-09-18 instance (as-of time + source sha256). Root cause: cron/refresh_v3_pages.sh rewrites docs/coverage.json on every run (v3.web.coverage_public) and renders those surfaces from it, but its `git add` list did not name the file; the nightly gates read the working tree, so they stayed green while every refresh commit was inconsistent in a fresh checkout (check_coverage_consistency: 285 findings on a clean clone of main 46832138 and of the first candidate 5f1f0422; OK on the production working copy). Repair: the file is in the refresh's staging block; tools/deploy_verify.py waits for it like every other artifact; docs/coverage.json of this tree is the 2026-09-18 file, reproduced byte for byte by the unmodified generator from the source instance whose sha256 the 81 committed surfaces name (no value typed, no check changed). Regression: tests/test_refresh_staging_fresh_checkout.py executes the script's marked staging block verbatim in a disposable repository (real generator, real commit, real clone, unmodified gate, real scoring universe), proves the original list fails in the clone while its working tree is green, and checks this checkout's own committed site. Limits: the surface renderers need the research node and are stood in by writers that bind through coverage_public.read(); the fix reaches the public endpoint only when this patch is on main — until then each refresh of main repeats the omission, and a candidate that merges such a refresh restages the file the same way. packaging.json and the scorecards in this directory describe the verification build of the first candidate source 4e792c97 and are kept as recorded; the sdist of the final candidate differs from that build in docs/ (this file's subject and the 8.0.1 change list).
additional_findings_not_counted.X02: the README's 'v7 — check → reproduce …' output block was recorded on the 7.0.0 candidate and had been relabelled by each version step; the sentence now says where it was recorded.
